A.parent_name: Formal salutation and signature block present
A.name: Identified accountable author with stated standing
A.instruction: Score whether the text names the author or organisation and states a role, occupation, expertise, or regulated relationship to the rule's subject that lets a reader weigh its claims. Score 10 when both are present (for example, 'I have operated a licensed facility of this type for eleven years'). Score 5 when standing is asserted vaguely, naming no role, activity, or relationship. Score 0 when nothing establishes the writer's relation to the rule; salutations, signature blocks, titles, and letterhead never count.
A.why_separable: A letter opening 'Dear Administrator' and closing with a typed name and title but never saying what the writer does scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling, while an unsigned first-person account from a named permit holder describing their own operation scores high here and 0 there.
A.original_name: Identified accountable author with stated standing
A.original_instruction: Score whether the comment establishes who is speaking and what experience or position backs what it says. Score 10 when the text names the author or organisation AND states a role, occupation, expertise, or regulated relationship to the subject of the rule that a reader can use to weigh the claims (for example, 'I have operated a licensed facility of this type for eleven years', 'we are the trade association whose members hold these permits'). Score 5 when standing is asserted but left vague ('an interested professional', 'a concerned industry group') with no role, activity, or relationship named. Score 0 when nothing in the text establishes who the writer is relative to the rule, no matter how formally the letter is addressed or signed. Ignore salutations, signature blocks, titles after a name, and letterhead entirely: they are not standing.

A.name: Numbers tied to a stated consequence for this rule
A.instruction: Score whether the comment's figures are attached to an identified provision with a stated step from figure to conclusion. Score 10 when a figure's source is shown and the comment states what it implies for that provision ('the proposed 30-day window covers 4,200 filings at 6 staff-hours each, 25,200 hours the rule does not account for'). Score 5 when a sourced, relevant figure's inference to the rule stays implicit. Score 0 when no figure is linked by stated reasoning to a provision, however dense the statistics and cited reports.
A.why_separable: A comment reciting fifteen sourced national statistics and then asserting a conclusion without connecting any of them to a provision scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling; a single self-reported operating figure worked through to a specific effect on the rule scores high here and low there.
A.upstream_parent: professional advocacy research and briefing support
A.original_name: Numbers tied to a stated consequence for this rule
A.original_instruction: Score whether quantities in the comment are actually put to work on the proposed rule. Score 10 when the comment's figures are each attached to an identified provision and the comment states what the number implies for that provision, showing where the figure came from and the step from figure to conclusion (for example, 'the proposed 30-day window applies to roughly 4,200 of our annual filings, at the 6 staff-hours per filing we currently log, which is 25,200 hours the rule does not account for'). Score 5 when a figure is relevant and sourced but the inference to the rule is left implicit. Score 0 when the comment contains no figure that is connected by stated reasoning to a provision of the rule, including the case where it is dense with statistics, dollar amounts and cited reports that are simply asserted alongside a position. Score the reasoning link, not the quantity, precision, or prestige of the sources.

A.name: Specific legal defect identified with authority and cure
A.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a legal defect specifically enough to be acted on. Score 10 when it names the particular statute, regulation, or procedural requirement, states what it requires, explains how the proposal departs from it, and states the change to the proposed text that would cure the departure. Score 5 when an authority is named and a conflict described but the mechanism or the cure is missing. Score 0 when unlawfulness or procedural defect is asserted without identifying which authority conflicts and how. Judge specificity only, not whether the legal argument is correct.
A.why_separable: A comment saying 'this rule is arbitrary and capricious, exceeds the agency's statutory authority, and we reserve all rights' with no provision named scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling; a plainly worded comment that quotes the enabling statute's definition, shows the proposed definition is wider, and proposes conforming text scores 10 here and low there.
A.original_name: Specific legal defect identified with authority and cure
A.original_instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a legal problem with enough specificity that the agency could act on it. Score 10 when the comment names the particular statutory section, regulation, or procedural requirement at issue, states its operative language or requirement, explains concretely how the proposal departs from it, and states the change to the proposed text that would resolve the departure. Score 5 when a specific authority is named and a conflict described, but the mechanism of the conflict or the requested cure is left unstated. Score 0 when the comment asserts that the rule is unlawful, unauthorised, arbitrary, or procedurally defective without identifying which authority it conflicts with and how, however forcefully the assertion is made. Score only the specificity of the identified defect and cure; do not judge whether the legal argument would ultimately prevail.

A.name: First-hand operational and engineering particulars
A.instruction: Score whether the comment supplies concrete technical or operational particulars drawn from hands-on work with the equipment, process, or facility the rule governs, tied to the requirement. Score 10 for specifics only such involvement yields: part or configuration numbers and what differs about them, observed failure or inspection findings and their frequency, actual labour hours or downtime, a conflict with an existing manual or procedure, an interval unmeetable for a stated physical reason. Score 5 when particulars are generic to the industry rather than the writer's own operation. Score 0 when no observed particular appears, however precisely rule paragraphs are cited.
A.why_separable: A tidy numbered list of citations each ending in 'we object to this paragraph' supplies no particulars and scores 0 here while scoring 10 on the sibling; a single unstructured paragraph describing what an inspection actually found on a fleet of aircraft scores high here and 0 there.
A.upstream_parent: the submitter is a regulated entity's engineering/compliance staff responding to a routine Airworthiness Directive or product-specific technical requirement as an established business process, not an independent stakeholder building a persuasive case
A.original_instruction: Score whether the comment supplies concrete technical or operational particulars that come from working with the equipment, process, or facility the rule governs. Score 10 when it reports specifics that could only be known from hands-on involvement and ties them to the requirement: part or configuration numbers and what differs about them, observed failure or inspection findings and their frequency, actual labour hours or downtime a procedure takes, a conflict between the proposed step and an existing manual or procedure, a compliance interval that cannot be met for a stated physical reason. Score 5 when technical particulars are present but generic to the industry rather than drawn from the writer's own operation. Score 0 when the comment states positions about the requirement, however precisely it names rule paragraphs and section numbers, without supplying any observed technical or operational particular. Score the particulars supplied, not the format they are presented in.

A.name: Substance carried over from the prior interaction
A.instruction: Score whether the comment reports actual content from earlier dealings and applies it to this proposal. Score 10 when it states what was specifically learned, tested, agreed, required, or observed earlier and uses it as evidence about this rule ('the weekly sampling required by our 2022 authorisation produced no exceedances over 18 months, which bears on the frequency proposed here'). Score 5 when earlier work is described generally and only loosely tied to a provision. Score 0 when prior meetings, submissions, or collaboration are referenced but nothing from them is reported or brought to bear.
A.why_separable: A comment that name-drops meetings and staff contacts but reports nothing from them scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling; a comment that reports detailed results of an earlier pilot without saying who at the agency was involved scores high here and low there.
A.upstream_parent: Existing relationships and insider access within the agency or docket lifecycle
A.original_name: Substance carried over from the prior interaction
A.original_instruction: Score whether the comment brings forward actual content from earlier dealings and applies it to the present proposal. Score 10 when it reports what was specifically learned, tested, agreed, required, or observed in the earlier interaction and uses it as evidence about this rule (for example, 'the monitoring condition imposed in our 2022 authorisation required weekly sampling; over 18 months it produced no exceedances, which bears on the sampling frequency proposed here'). Score 5 when earlier work is described in general terms and only loosely connected to a provision. Score 0 when prior meetings, submissions, or collaboration are referred to but nothing from them is reported or brought to bear on the proposal — including the case where the comment says 'as we discussed with your staff' and then argues from scratch. Score only what the text actually carries over.

A.name: Documented experience complying with the existing requirements
A.instruction: Score whether the comment reports concrete experience of operating under the agency's current requirements and uses it to say how the proposal would work. Score 10 when it describes what compliance actually involved, such as steps performed, time or cost incurred, review timelines encountered, obstacles or workarounds, and connects that record to a specific effect of the proposed change. Score 5 when compliance experience is described but tied to no provision. Score 0 when nothing about what complying entailed is reported, or the proposal is discussed purely in the abstract; a relationship with the agency is not experience.
A.why_separable: A comment stating 'we hold three permits from your agency and have met with your staff annually' and then arguing generically scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling; a detailed account of what a permit renewal actually required, from an author who never says they hold one, still scores high here and 0 there.
A.upstream_parent: existing relationships with agency personnel or programs
A.original_name: Documented experience complying with the existing requirements
A.original_instruction: Score whether the comment reports concrete experience of operating under the agency's current requirements and uses it to say how the proposal would work. Score 10 when it describes what compliance actually involved — the steps performed, the time or cost incurred, the review timelines encountered, the obstacles or workarounds that arose — and connects that record to a specific effect the proposed change would have. Score 5 when compliance experience is described but not connected to any provision of the proposal. Score 0 when the comment establishes a history with the agency without reporting anything about what complying entailed, or discusses the proposal purely in the abstract. Score the reported experience and its application; the existence of a relationship is not itself experience.

A.parent_name: Formal institutional filing apparatus / letterhead conventions
A.name: Provision-by-provision engagement with the proposed text
A.instruction: Score how precisely the comment engages the content of particular proposed provisions. Score 10 when it identifies the specific provisions it addresses, states what each would require, and gives a reason directed at that requirement, so a reader can tell which parts it is about and what it says about each. Score 5 when it engages the proposal's substance only at the level of the rulemaking as a whole, without separating provisions. Score 0 when it expresses support, opposition, or general subject-area discussion without engaging what any particular provision would require; a docket or RIN citation in a caption is not engagement.
A.why_separable: A letter on letterhead with a full 'Re: Docket No. …' caption, membership footnotes, and a titled signature whose body is two sentences of general support scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling; an unformatted email that walks through three proposed paragraphs and what each would require scores 10 here and 0 there.
A.upstream_parent: the comment was drafted by professional legal counsel, in-house regulatory/tax staff, or a paid lobbyist following standard formal rulemaking-filing conventions
A.original_name: Provision-by-provision engagement with the proposed text
A.original_instruction: Score how precisely the comment engages the actual content of the proposal. Score 10 when it identifies the particular proposed provisions it addresses, states what each of those provisions would require, and gives a reason directed at that requirement — so a reader can tell which parts of the rule the comment is about and what it says about each. Score 5 when it engages the proposal's substance but only at the level of the rulemaking as a whole, without separating provisions. Score 0 when the comment expresses support or opposition, or discusses the general subject area, without engaging what any particular proposed provision would require — including comments that cite the docket or RIN number in a caption and then never return to the rule's contents. A caption, footnote, or citation is not engagement; only discussion of what the provisions would do counts.

A.name: Aggregated first-hand evidence from the represented population
A.instruction: Score whether the comment reports what is actually observed across the population it speaks for and applies it to the rule. Score 10 for pooled or patterned evidence, such as survey results, recurring case types and how often they arise, ranges of practice across members, documented incidents, or variation between large and small participants, stated to imply a specific effect of the proposal. Score 5 for one or two concrete instances from its constituency, with no pattern established and no provision attached. Score 0 when breadth of members, customers, or dollars is claimed but nothing observed across them is reported.
A.why_separable: A comment opening 'as the nation's largest association, representing 12,000 members and $400 billion in assets' and then arguing purely from principle scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling; a small unnamed cooperative reporting how the requirement played out across its eleven sites scores high here and 0 there.
A.upstream_parent: submitter resources, status, and perceived agency importance
A.original_name: Aggregated first-hand evidence from the represented population
A.original_instruction: Score whether the comment reports what is actually observed across the population it speaks for, and applies it to the rule. Score 10 when it conveys pooled or patterned evidence from that population — survey results, recurring case types and how often they arise, ranges of practice across members, documented incidents, variation between large and small participants — and states what that evidence implies for a specific effect of the proposal. Score 5 when it reports one or two concrete instances from its constituency without establishing a pattern or connecting it to a provision. Score 0 when the comment asserts that it represents many members, customers, or dollars but reports nothing observed across them, arguing instead from general principle or assertion. Breadth of representation claimed is not evidence; only reported observation counts.

A.name: Reconciles conflicting evidence rather than citing one side
A.instruction: Score whether the comment engages evidence pointing against its own position. Score 10 when it states what the contrary evidence is and explains how to reconcile it with the position the comment takes. Score 5 when contrary evidence is acknowledged but left unreconciled. Score 0 when only supporting evidence is presented. Judge the engagement with conflicting evidence, not which side of the question is right.
A.original_name: Reconciles conflicting evidence rather than citing one side
A.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment acknowledges evidence pointing the other way and explains how to reconcile it with its own position. Score 0 when only supporting evidence is presented. Judge whether conflicting evidence is engaged.

A.name: Specifies how compliance would be demonstrated in practice
A.instruction: Score whether the comment says concretely what a regulated party would have to record, measure, or show to demonstrate compliance, either under the proposal or under the comment's own alternative. Score 10 when the records, measurements, or showings are named specifically enough that a reader could carry them out. Score 5 when demonstration is mentioned only in general terms. Score 0 when how compliance would be demonstrated is not addressed. Judge the concreteness of the demonstration described, not whether it would be workable.
A.original_name: Specifies how compliance would be demonstrated in practice
A.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment says concretely what a regulated party would have to record, measure or show to demonstrate compliance under the proposal or under its own alternative. Score 0 when compliance demonstration is not addressed. Judge the concreteness of the demonstration described.

B.parent_name: Formal salutation and signature block present
B.name: Letter furniture: salutation and signature block
B.instruction: Score only the presence of formal letter furniture, a surface feature of the document. Score 10 when the comment both opens with a formal salutation ('Dear Administrator', 'To Whom It May Concern') and closes with a signature block naming a person or organisation, usually with a complimentary close ('Sincerely,'). Score 5 when exactly one of the two is present, and 0 when neither is. Do not read the body: a blank form letter with both scores 10, and a comment that begins mid-argument and ends without a sign-off scores 0.
B.why_separable: A mass-campaign postcard with the salutation and sign-off filled in and no content scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.
B.original_name: Letter furniture: salutation and signature block
B.original_instruction: Score only the presence of formal letter furniture. Score 10 when the comment both opens with a formal salutation ('Dear Administrator', 'Dear Sir or Madam', 'To Whom It May Concern') and closes with a signature block naming a person or organisation, typically with a complimentary close ('Sincerely,', 'Respectfully submitted,'). Score 5 when exactly one of the two is present. Score 0 when neither is present. This is a formatting judgement: score the salutation and signature block as text objects and nothing else. Do not read the body. A blank form letter with a salutation and a signature block scores 10; a detailed, expert, substantive comment that begins mid-argument and ends without a sign-off scores 0.

B.name: Density of figures, citations and named sources
B.instruction: Score the amount of quantified and attributed material visible in the text, a surface feature scored without regard to accuracy, relevance, or use. Score 10 when precise statistics, dollar amounts, percentages, numerical forecasts, named studies or reports, cited authorities, and links or footnotes appear repeatedly throughout. Score 5 for a few scattered figures or one or two named sources. Score 0 when the text contains no numbers and names no external source. Count what appears on the page: numbers that go nowhere still count, and figure-free qualitative reasoning scores 0.
B.why_separable: A purely qualitative first-hand account that reasons precisely about the rule's effects without citing a single number scores 0 here and can score high on the sibling only if it has figures, so the clearest separator is the number-dense comment that argues nothing.
B.upstream_parent: professional advocacy research and briefing support
B.original_name: Density of figures, citations and named sources
B.original_instruction: Score the amount of quantified and attributed material visible in the text, without judging its accuracy, relevance, or use. Score 10 when the comment is thick with such material: precise statistics, dollar amounts, percentages, numerical forecasts, named studies or reports, cited authorities, and links or footnotes, appearing repeatedly throughout. Score 5 for a few scattered figures or one or two named sources. Score 0 when the comment contains no numbers and names no external source. Count what appears on the page. A comment that piles up impressive-looking numbers that go nowhere scores 10; a carefully reasoned qualitative comment with no figures scores 0.

B.name: Adversarial legal register and violation language
B.instruction: Score how strongly the text adopts the vocabulary and posture of an adversarial legal filing, scored as register and independent of any argument. Score 10 when it is saturated with legal-conflict language: 'arbitrary and capricious', 'unlawful', 'exceeds statutory authority', 'violates the plain text', 'fails to satisfy notice-and-comment requirements', 'we reserve all rights', demands that the agency withdraw or rescind, warnings of legal jeopardy or challenge. Score 5 when one such formulation appears inside otherwise ordinary prose. Score 0 when no legal-violation or legal-remedy language appears; do not check whether any cited provision exists or whether the characterisation is apt.
B.why_separable: Boilerplate objection language with no identified provision scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.
B.original_name: Adversarial legal register and violation language
B.original_instruction: Score how strongly the comment adopts the vocabulary and posture of an adversarial legal filing, independent of any argument. Score 10 when the text is saturated with legal-conflict register: phrases such as 'arbitrary and capricious', 'unlawful', 'exceeds statutory authority', 'violates the plain text', 'fails to satisfy notice-and-comment requirements', 'we reserve all rights', formal demands that the agency withdraw or rescind, and warnings of legal jeopardy or challenge. Score 5 when one such formulation appears inside otherwise ordinary prose. Score 0 when no legal-violation or legal-remedy language appears at all. Score the register and the demands as they appear on the page; do not check whether any cited provision exists or whether the characterisation is apt.

B.name: Addressee-directed numbered items with rule-citation tags
B.instruction: Score the layout of the document, a surface feature. Score 10 when the comment is addressed to a named official or office and its body is broken into discrete numbered or lettered items, each anchored to a citation tag such as a rule paragraph, CFR subsection, Airworthiness Directive number, docket number, or service-bulletin reference, with little connective persuasive narrative between items. Score 5 when it is partly itemised, itemised without citation tags, or tagged without itemisation. Score 0 for continuous persuasive prose with no addressee-directed itemisation keyed to rule sections. Items that say nothing substantive still score 10.
B.why_separable: A form-structured compliance response whose numbered items are empty concurrences scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.
B.upstream_parent: the submitter is a regulated entity's engineering/compliance staff responding to a routine Airworthiness Directive or product-specific technical requirement as an established business process, not an independent stakeholder building a persuasive case
B.original_name: Addressee-directed numbered items with rule-citation tags
B.original_instruction: Score the layout of the comment. Score 10 when it is addressed to a named official or office and its body is broken into discrete numbered or lettered items, each anchored to a specific citation tag such as a rule paragraph, CFR subsection, Airworthiness Directive number, docket number, or service-bulletin reference, with little connective persuasive narrative between the items. Score 5 when it is partially itemised, or itemised without citation tags, or tagged without itemisation. Score 0 when it is continuous persuasive prose with no addressee-directed itemised structure keyed to rule sections. This scores document structure and citation tagging only; the content of the items is irrelevant, and an itemised list whose entries say nothing substantive still scores 10.

B.name: Mentions of prior contact with the agency
B.instruction: Score how much the text signals an existing relationship with the agency, counting the references themselves. Score 10 when it refers explicitly and repeatedly to prior meetings, ongoing collaboration, earlier submissions, established partnerships, working groups, or direct exchanges with named agency personnel. Score 5 for a single passing reference to previous contact. Score 0 when the comment carries only a generic address to the agency and mentions no relationship history. Do not consider whether the relationship described adds anything to the comment.
B.why_separable: A brief note consisting mainly of 'further to our meeting with your office last month and our prior comments on this docket' scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.
B.upstream_parent: Existing relationships and insider access within the agency or docket lifecycle
B.original_name: Mentions of prior contact with the agency
B.original_instruction: Score how much the comment signals an existing relationship with the agency. Score 10 when it refers explicitly and repeatedly to prior meetings, ongoing collaboration, earlier submissions, established partnerships, working groups, or direct exchanges with named agency personnel. Score 5 for a single passing reference to previous contact. Score 0 when the comment carries only a generic address to the agency and mentions no relationship history. Score the presence and frequency of these references as they appear in the text; do not consider whether the relationship they describe adds anything to the comment.

B.name: Explicit disclosure of past dealings with agency
B.instruction: Score whether the writer explicitly discloses a prior or ongoing relationship with the agency, counting the disclosure as a textual feature. Score 10 when the comment states outright that it holds or has held permits, licences, contracts, or authorisations from the agency, or describes recurring meetings, ongoing communications, or past dealings with it. Score 5 for an oblique or single-clause reference to earlier contact. Score 0 when no prior agency relationship is mentioned anywhere in the text. Whether the disclosed relationship lends authority, and whether anything follows from it, are outside this criterion.
B.why_separable: A one-line submission that discloses two prior permits and nothing else scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.
B.upstream_parent: existing relationships with agency personnel or programs
B.original_name: Explicit disclosure of past dealings with agency
B.original_instruction: Score whether the writer explicitly discloses a prior or ongoing relationship with the agency. Score 10 when the comment states outright that it holds or has held permits, licences, contracts, or authorisations from the agency, or describes recurring meetings, ongoing communications, or past dealings with it. Score 5 for an oblique or single-clause reference to earlier contact. Score 0 when no prior agency relationship is mentioned anywhere in the text. This scores the presence of the disclosure as a textual feature only; whether the disclosed relationship lends the writer authority, and whether anything follows from it, are outside this criterion.

B.parent_name: Formal institutional filing apparatus / letterhead conventions
B.name: Filing apparatus density
B.instruction: Score the density of formal filing conventions visible in the document, a formatting feature. Count: an addressee block naming an official or office and address; a 'Re:' or 'Subject:' caption carrying a docket, RIN, or file number; numbered footnotes, especially ones describing the organisation's membership, assets, or history; a formal salutation such as 'Dear Sir or Madam'; and a closing signature giving a name with a professional title. Score 10 when the full apparatus is present, 5 when one or two conventions appear, and 0 for plain conversational text carrying none. Never score what the document argues.
B.why_separable: A one-paragraph position letter wrapped in the complete counsel filing apparatus scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.
B.upstream_parent: the comment was drafted by professional legal counsel, in-house regulatory/tax staff, or a paid lobbyist following standard formal rulemaking-filing conventions
B.original_instruction: Score the density of formal filing conventions visible in the document. Count the presence of: an addressee block naming an official or office and address; a 'Re:' or 'Subject:' caption carrying a docket, RIN, or file number; numbered footnotes, especially ones describing the organisation's membership, assets, or history; a formal salutation such as 'Dear Sir or Madam'; and a closing signature giving a name with a professional title. Score 10 when the full apparatus is present. Score 5 when one or two of these conventions appear. Score 0 for plain conversational text carrying none of them. These are formatting conventions and this criterion scores their presence and completeness only — never what the document argues, and never whether the footnoted credentials are impressive.

B.name: Prominence of organizational size and prestige claims
B.instruction: Score how prominently the comment foregrounds its own organisational scale and standing. Score 10 when quantified membership, customer counts, assets under management, market share, national or multi-state reach, founding date, or prestige superlatives ('the largest', 'the nation's leading') are placed front and centre, typically in the opening paragraph or a credentialing footnote, and repeated. Score 5 when organisational size is mentioned once, in passing. Score 0 when no organisational-scale or prestige claim appears at all, including comments from individuals. Score these claims as text, never whether the claimed scale makes the argument stronger or the author better informed.
B.why_separable: A two-sentence comment consisting of a scale-and-prestige self-introduction plus a bare statement of opposition scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.
B.upstream_parent: submitter resources, status, and perceived agency importance
B.original_name: Prominence of organizational size and prestige claims
B.original_instruction: Score how much the comment foregrounds its own organisational scale and standing. Score 10 when quantified membership, customer counts, assets under management, market share, national or multi-state reach, founding date, or prestige superlatives ('the largest', 'the nation's leading', 'the oldest') are placed front and centre, typically in the opening paragraph or a credentialing footnote, and repeated. Score 5 when organisational size is mentioned once, in passing. Score 0 when the comment makes no organisational-scale or prestige claim at all, including comments from individuals. Score the presence and prominence of these claims as text; never score whether the claimed scale makes the comment's argument stronger or its author better informed.

B.name: Deadline, extension, and re-opened-period timing language
B.instruction: Score how much the text explicitly orients itself to the clock of the comment period, counting only language about the filing window and never compliance deadlines proposed inside the rule. Markers: naming the closing date; asserting timeliness ('submitted prior to the close of the comment period'); noting the hour or channel of filing; requesting an extension; identifying the document as supplemental, amended, corrected, or a re-submission; invoking a re-opened or extended window. Score 10 for several such moves, prominently placed; 5 for exactly one passing reference; 0 when nothing anywhere addresses dates, deadlines, timeliness, extensions, or an earlier filing by this same commenter. Ignore references to what other parties have filed.
B.upstream_parent: Where the comment's filing timestamp falls relative to the opening and closing of the comment period, including whether it landed in an extended, re-opened, or post-deadline window.
B.original_name: Deadline, extension, and re-opened-period timing language
B.original_instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the text explicitly orients itself to the clock of the comment period. Count only language about the FILING WINDOW, not compliance deadlines proposed inside the rule. Markers that count: naming the closing date; asserting timeliness ('submitted prior to the close of the comment period'); noting the hour or channel of filing; requesting an extension or additional time; identifying the document as supplemental, amended, corrected, or a re-submission; or invoking a re-opened or extended comment window. 10 = several such moves, prominent, often in the opening or closing paragraph. 5 = exactly one passing reference (e.g., a bare 'timely filed' or a date line tied to the deadline). 0 = nothing anywhere about dates, deadlines, timeliness, extensions, or an earlier filing by this same commenter; the text could have been written on any day of the period. Do not score references to what OTHER parties have filed (that is a different channel).

B.name: Awareness of the accumulated docket record
B.instruction: Score how much the comment shows that a record already existed when it was written. Markers: naming, quoting, characterizing, or rebutting other commenters; responding to arguments raised by others in the docket; citing a hearing, listening session, or roundtable already held; referring to a coalition, sign-on, or joint letter already submitted; citing the agency's own post-proposal actions; citing outside developments that post-date the proposal. Score 10 when the comment is built substantially around such material, with two or more distinct references to things that happened after publication; 5 for one clear reference in an otherwise self-contained comment; 0 when only the proposed rule and the commenter's own material are engaged. Citations to prior rulemakings, statutes, case law, or academic literature predating the proposal do not count.
B.upstream_parent: Late ordinal position in the sequence of filings, and long elapsed time since the docket opened, so that a public record and post-proposal developments were available to read and cite.
B.original_name: Awareness of the accumulated docket record
B.original_instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the comment shows that a record already existed when it was written. Markers: naming, quoting, characterizing, or rebutting other commenters; responding to arguments 'raised by others in this docket'; citing testimony or statements from a public hearing, listening session, or roundtable already held; referring to a coalition, sign-on, or joint letter already submitted; citing the agency's own post-proposal actions (a supplemental notice, correction, data release, FAQ, or answers to earlier submissions); or citing outside developments that post-date the proposal ('in the nine months since the NPRM issued, ...'). 10 = the comment is substantially built around such material, with two or more distinct references to things that happened after the rule was published. 5 = one clear reference, otherwise self-contained. 0 = the comment engages only the proposed rule and the commenter's own material, with no sign that anything has occurred since publication. Do NOT count citations to prior rulemakings, statutes, case law, or academic literature that predate the proposal; those show expertise, not record awareness.

B.name: De novo issue scaffolding versus incorporation by reference
B.instruction: Score how much the comment builds its issue from the ground up, as though nothing has been said yet, rather than attaching itself to another party's submission. Score 10 for fully de novo scaffolding: it restates what the rule proposes, supplies its own framing and definitions of key terms, introduces the commenter and their stake at length, walks through background the agency already knows, and adopts, endorses, echoes, or incorporates no other filing. Score 5 for mostly standalone framing with a brief nod to another filing or one 'we agree with' aside. Score 0 for a follower move such as 'we join and incorporate by reference the comments of X', with little or no standalone framing. Judge framing posture only, not correctness or writing quality.
B.upstream_parent: Early ordinal position in the filing sequence: little or nothing was in the record at drafting time, so there was nothing available to endorse, join, or incorporate.
B.original_name: De novo issue scaffolding versus incorporation by reference
B.original_instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the comment builds its issue from the ground up as though nothing has been said yet, as opposed to attaching itself to something already said. 10 = fully de novo scaffolding: it restates or summarizes what the rule proposes, supplies its own framing and definitions of key terms, introduces the commenter and their stake at length, walks through background the agency already knows, and contains NO adoption, endorsement, echo, or incorporation of another party's submission. 5 = mostly standalone but with a brief nod to another filing, or standalone framing plus one 'we agree with' aside. 0 = a pure follower move, e.g. 'we join and incorporate by reference the comments of X', 'we adopt the analysis submitted by Y and write only to add one point', 'we endorse the coalition letter' — little or no standalone framing of the issue. Judge only the framing posture, not whether the analysis is correct or the writing is good.

B.name: Mass-campaign petition register
B.instruction: Score how strongly the text reads as one voice in an organised mass-participation drive rather than an individually composed submission to a decisionmaker. Markers: template or boilerplate phrasing with a small personalised insert; crowd framing ('I join the thousands of Americans', 'add my name'); calls for the reader or others to act, sign, or share; head-count or vote-count framing; slogan or campaign-title language; a single short paragraph of sentiment with no rule-specific detail, citation, or factual claim; a salutation addressed to a cause or the public rather than the agency. Score 10 for several such markers, unmistakably a campaign artifact; 5 for individually written but clearly campaign-prompted text; 0 for rule-specific, individualised text addressed to the agency. Do not score the position taken.
B.upstream_parent: The comment sits in a large, high-salience, mass-participation docket where an advocacy campaign drove filings, so docket size is enormous relative to a specialist rulemaking.
B.original_instruction: Score 0-10 on how strongly the text reads as one voice in an organized mass-participation drive rather than an individually composed submission to a decisionmaker. Markers: template or form-letter phrasing and boilerplate blocks with a small personalized insert; explicit crowd framing ('I join the thousands of Americans', 'add my name'); direct calls for the reader or others to act, sign, or share; head-count or vote-count framing ('count me among those opposed', 'the public has spoken'); slogan or campaign-title language; a single short paragraph of personal sentiment with no rule-specific detail, section citation, or factual claim; salutation addressed to a cause or to the public rather than to the agency. 10 = several of these, unmistakably a campaign artifact. 5 = individually written but clearly campaign-prompted (e.g., recites a campaign talking point and urges others to comment). 0 = no campaign markers at all: rule-specific, individualized, addressed to the agency as a decisionmaker. Do not reward or penalize the position taken.

B.name: Specialist insider shorthand assuming a small expert readership
B.instruction: Score how strongly the text presumes a small, already-expert readership. Markers: program acronyms and technical shorthand unexpanded at first use; bare citation of sections, paragraphs, tables, or preamble page numbers with no explanation; direct address to a named office, division, docket manager, or staff contact; casual cross-reference to other dockets, prior rulemakings, meetings, or ex parte contacts as shared history, including assumed familiarity with the commenter and their role; jargon-dense sentences with no lay gloss. Score 10 when this is pervasive and a general reader could not follow without a glossary; 5 for a mixed register with key terms explained; 0 when everything is spelled out for a lay reader. Score the assumed audience only, not whether the technical content is correct.
B.upstream_parent: The comment sits in a small specialist docket with few filers, where the writer expects a handful of agency technical staff — not a general public — to read it.
B.original_name: Specialist insider shorthand assuming a small expert readership
B.original_instruction: Score 0-10 for how strongly the text presumes a small, already-expert readership. Markers: program acronyms and technical shorthand used without expansion at first use; bare citation of sections, paragraphs, tables, or preamble page numbers with no explanation of what they are; direct address to a named office, division, docket manager, or staff contact; casual cross-reference to other dockets, prior rulemakings, meetings, or ex parte contacts as though the reader shares that history; jargon-dense sentences with no lay gloss; assumption that the reader already knows the commenter and their role. 10 = pervasive — a general reader could not follow the comment without a glossary. 5 = mixed register, some shorthand but key terms explained. 0 = everything is spelled out for a lay reader: acronyms expanded, the program and the proposal explained from scratch, no assumed shared history, no named-staff address. Score the ASSUMED AUDIENCE only, not whether the technical content is correct.

B.name: Attachment or exhibit is referenced
B.instruction: Score only whether the text refers to an attached document, exhibit, appendix, or enclosure. Score 10 when at least one such reference appears anywhere in the comment. Score 0 when it refers to none. Score the reference itself as a surface feature, never the content of the attachment.
B.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment refers to an attached document, exhibit, appendix or enclosure. Score 0 when it refers to none. Score only the reference, never the content of the attachment.

B.name: Comment is shorter than three sentences
B.instruction: Score only the comment's sentence count. Score 10 when the comment consists of fewer than three sentences, that is one or two. Score 0 when it consists of three or more. Count sentences as written, regardless of their length, content, or quality.
B.original_name: Comment is shorter than three sentences
B.original_instruction: Score 10 when the comment consists of fewer than three sentences. Score 0 when it is longer. Score only the sentence count.
